summary: Describes an Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP) mapping for provisioning and managing organization objects stored in a shared central repository. EPP is used by domain registries and registrars. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Domain registries keep records about domains and people. This document adds a record type for companies and other organizations so they can be stored and managed the same way.

questions: how to manage organizations in a registry
what is the epp organization mapping
what role types does epp organization support
subtitle: A new EPP object type so registries can record registrars, resellers, privacy proxies and DNS operators as organizations.

tldr.problem: Registrars, resellers, DNS service operators and privacy proxies take part in domain registration, but EPP had no formal object for them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8543 defines an XML organization object with roles, statuses, an optional parent link, postal and contact data, and maps the EPP check, info, create, delete and update commands onto it.
tldr.outcome: Registries can store and manage these organizations in a shared central repository in a uniform way. A new IANA registry lists the allowed role types.

today: RFC 8543 is a Proposed Standard from March 2019. The unit metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC, so it remains the definition of the EPP organization mapping.

sections.title: Why Organizations Need an Object
sections.content:
Many kinds of entities are involved in the domain registration business: registrars, resellers, DNS service operators and privacy proxies. The RFC says these have not been formally defined as having an object in the Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP). RFC 8543 provides a way to describe them as organization entities.

The document is an organization object mapping for version 1.0 of EPP, which is defined in RFC 5730. It is written in XML 1.0 with XML Schema notation. Elements use the prefix org for the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:epp:org-1.0, but implementations MUST NOT depend on the prefix.
sections.plainLanguage: Registries already had cards for domains and for people, but not for the companies that help sell domains. This document makes a card for them.

sections.title: Attributes of an Organization Object
sections.content:
Every organization has a server-unique identifier in <org:id>, which uses the clIDType syntax from RFC 5730. An organization MUST always have at least one role (<org:role>). A role has a required type, optional statuses and an optional <org:roleID>, a third-party-assigned identifier such as the IANA ID for registrars. One organization may hold several roles with different types. Only the sponsoring client can set roles.

Other attributes include a postal address (up to two <org:postalInfo> elements, one internationalized and one localized), voice and fax numbers, an email address, a web home page in <org:url>, and contact identifiers. Contact types are admin, tech, billing, abuse and custom. Dates and times MUST be in UTC in the extended XML Schema form with uppercase T and Z.

Organizations can have more than one layer through <org:parentId>. In the reseller example, the top-level reseller is the registrar of the registry and has no parent. An N-tier reseller has a parent reseller and at least one child reseller. Loops MUST be prohibited, so if A has B as parent, B cannot have A as parent, and the same holds for larger loops.
sections.plainLanguage: Each organization card has a name, an address, a phone number and a list of jobs it does. A card can also point to a bigger company above it, but the pointing can never go in a circle.

sections.title: Statuses on Organizations and Roles
sections.content:
An organization MUST always have at least one status. Statuses prefixed client can be set by the sponsoring client, and statuses prefixed server by the server. A client MUST NOT alter server status values, while a server MAY override client ones under local policy.

  • ok is the normal state, set and removed by the server.
  • hold and terminated mean transform commands and new links MUST be rejected. A terminated organization MUST NOT be linked.
  • linked means at least one active association exists. It is not set by the client.
  • clientLinkProhibited and serverLinkProhibited reject new links.
  • clientUpdateProhibited, serverUpdateProhibited, clientDeleteProhibited and serverDeleteProhibited block updates and deletes.
  • pendingCreate, pendingUpdate and pendingDelete mean a command was processed but the action is not complete.

Some combinations are restricted. pendingCreate, ok, hold and terminated are mutually exclusive, and exactly one of them MUST be set. ok may only be combined with linked. The three pending statuses MUST NOT be combined with each other. Roles have their own, smaller set: ok, linked, clientLinkProhibited and serverLinkProhibited.
sections.plainLanguage: Each card has little stickers such as normal, on hold or do not delete. Some stickers only the registry may place, and some can be mixed while others cannot.

sections.title: How the EPP Commands Work
sections.content:
The mapping covers query and transform commands. <check> takes one or more ids and returns an avail value per id (1 or true means it can be provisioned), with an optional <org:reason>. <info> takes one id and returns the full object, including the repository object identifier (<org:roid>), roles, statuses, parent, contacts and creation and update data.

<create> builds an organization and returns its id and creation date. <delete> removes it, but an organization MUST NOT be deleted while it is associated with other known objects, and the server MUST answer with error code 2305 in that case. <update> uses <org:add>, <org:rem> and <org:chg>. A change to postal info replaces that whole element, and an empty one removes that type.

No mapping is defined for <transfer> or <renew>, since transfer and renewal semantics do not apply to organizations.
sections.plainLanguage: You can ask whether a card name is free, read a card, make one, change one or throw one away. You cannot move a card to someone else or renew it, because that makes no sense for a company card.

sections.title: Offline Review and Pending Actions
sections.content:
Transform commands are normally completed in real time. A server operator MAY defer completion when human or third-party review is needed. In that case the server MUST return response code 1001, which says the command was received and processed but the action is pending, and MUST reflect this in the object's status.

When the action finishes, the client MUST be notified by a service message that the action is complete and the status has changed. Other notification methods MAY be used in addition.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes a person has to look at your request before it is finished. The registry tells you it got the request, and later sends a note saying it is done.

sections.title: IANA Registrations and the Role Registry
sections.content:
IANA assigned the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:epp:org-1.0 and the schema urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:epp:org-1.0, and registered the extension in the EPP extensions registry.

IANA also created a new registry named "EPP Organization Role Values" with the registration policy Expert Review. The initial values are registrar (the authority responsible for the registration in the registry), reseller (a third party through which the registration was conducted), privacyproxy (a third party who could help register a domain without exposing the registrants' private information) and dns-operator (a third-party DNS operator maintaining name servers and zone data for a registrant).
sections.plainLanguage: There is an official list of allowed jobs for a company card. It starts with four jobs, and new ones can be added after an expert looks at them.

sections.title: Privacy and Security
sections.content: An organization object may hold personally identifiable information such as <org:contact>. This information is not required and is provided voluntarily. If it is provided, client and server MUST ensure that authorization information is stored and exchanged with high-grade encryption mechanisms, as specified in RFC 5733. The security considerations of RFC 5730 and of the protocol layers EPP runs over also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: If a card has private details, they must be kept in a locked box and sent in a sealed envelope.

items.label: Registrar
items.desc: The authority responsible for the registration in the registry.

items.label: Reseller
items.desc: A third party through which the registration was conducted.

items.label: Privacy proxy
items.desc: A third party who could help register a domain without exposing the registrants' private information.

items.label: DNS operator
items.desc: A third-party DNS operator that maintains name servers and zone data for a registrant.
